goal: Add the smallest complete Telegram design checkpoint: detect interface intent, obtain a bounded advisory Codex design brief, require user confirmation, expose a configured Mini App entry, and preserve the reviewed Provider generation and delivery route.
acceptance_criteria: Interface and visual-redesign requests record Telegram Bot plus Telegram Mini App surfaces, mobile-first design constraints, direct screenshot/video evidence, and a user design-confirmation checkpoint.
A bounded, redacted, hashed CGKNCodexCapabilityEscalation is written to per-chat support state and recorded in agent_session.
When explicitly enabled, local codex.exe runs in ephemeral read-only mode and its draft is validated into an advisory brief before whiteboard projection.
Pending or unavailable Codex supervision remains visible as workflow state and never silently becomes an approved design.
Generation cannot start while required design supervision or user design confirmation is pending.
An HTTPS Mini App URL can be offered through a Telegram web_app button and web_app_data enters the existing intake path.
Non-visual short requests do not acquire interface scope or a Codex design checkpoint.
Provider output validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, and delivery_manifest remain the only Telegram generation and delivery route.

quality_metrics.measure: bounded design-supervision usefulness and authority isolation
quality_metrics.target: all prepared requests and completed briefs validate; no supervisor artifact has candidate, evidence, package, or delivery authority
quality_metrics.method: deterministic adapter tests plus Codex supervisor contract tests

quality_metrics.target: visual Telegram products freeze interaction surfaces, mobile-first/theme/accessibility requirements, and screenshot/video acceptance before generation
quality_metrics.method: whiteboard contract tests and Telegram message-path integration tests

quality_metrics.measure: formal Provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and Provider route guards pass without a second generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: kernel contract and formal Provider regression tests

prevention: Keep design detection and Codex handoff in a dedicated adapter; make only narrow Telegram intake and start-policy changes.
assurance: Review every new state field as workflow/support state rather than formal evidence.
Review the diff against the Telegram mainline and Codex authority contracts.
control: Run adapter, Telegram intake, Codex supervisor, and kernel contract tests.
Run a live read-only Codex smoke test only if it does not create or alter generated candidates.
improvement: Record whether design-first routing avoids the prior CLI-only scope error without increasing short-request complexity.

interface_expectations: analyze_design_intent(text, whiteboard) returns a deterministic support-state update without starting generation.
prepare_design_escalation(session_dir, chat_id, session) writes only bounded per-chat support artifacts and agent_session events.
A validated design brief is projected into whiteboard support state with advisory_only true and requires explicit user confirmation.
TelegramClient.send_message accepts an optional web_app button only for a validated HTTPS Mini App URL.
web_app_data is normalized to one user message and then follows handle_text.

feedback: The design checkpoint, bounded read-only Codex supervision, explicit user approval gate, Mini App entry contract, and unchanged Provider delivery route passed deterministic and full-repository verification. A real Codex CLI smoke produced a valid advisory brief. Live Telegram Mini App launch remains NOT_EVALUATED until a public HTTPS Mini App URL is configured.

worked: Separating one-function business scope from product interaction scope kept short requests minimal while correctly routing GUI requests through design confirmation.
Reusing the existing capability-supervisor seal and Provider revalidation preserved authority boundaries instead of adding a second generation path.
did_not_work: The first full regression exposed that the new test filename required the repository's Telegram profile marker; the actual runtime and design assertions were not failing.
experiments: Configure a public HTTPS Mini App URL and run one private-chat launch plus web_app_data round trip before treating live Telegram interaction as evaluated.
